correctness.rationale: PASS: Writing G=(a,h), fixed-point-free action makes 1-h invertible for all h≠1; every outside-kernel element belongs to a unique conjugate complement H_x. The equation for commutation of ((1-h)x,h) and ((1-k)y,k) simplifies to (1-h)(1-k)(x-y)=0, forcing x=y. Nonidentity kernel elements commute with no outside element, and same-prime restriction precludes within-P edges. Thus each complement forms exactly the join of prime-primary nonidentity discrete sets, with kernel isolated vertices. Integral join Künneth yields the homology and handles q_i=2 and r=1 boundaries. Conjugation gives affine permutation of complement labels with trivial internal homology action; H acts freely on nonzero kernel points, so the asserted integral modules, three-valued character and topological orbit space follow.

The affine/permutation integral module and precise isolated-orbit count convey more than a standard abstract group-theoretic Frobenius partition, and can be used to analyze conjugation quotients.

limitations: Requires a single-prime abelian kernel, cyclic complement, each nonidentity h fixed-point-free; not arbitrary Frobenius groups.
The r=1 case is discrete; a factor q_i=2 kills positive top homology; no sheaf homology.
